defects.title: Temporary files from interrupted writes are never cleaned up
defects.repro: DATA_FILE=/tmp/x/ledger.json PORT=<port> node server.js; POST /groups {"id":"g","members":["Ann","Bob"]}; from 8 clients loop POST /groups/g/expenses {"payer":"Ann","cents":2,"split":"equal"}; send SIGKILL to the server after ~200 ms; ls /tmp/x; start the server again with the same DATA_FILE, stop it, ls /tmp/x
defects.observed: A file ledger.json.<uuid>.tmp holding a partial or full ledger sits beside ledger.json and remains after the restart (3 of 5 rounds); ledger.json itself parses and is complete
defects.expected: Stray temporary files from an interrupted write removed at startup (or never left), so the data directory does not accumulate copies of the ledger

defects.title: A crash during a write leaves an orphan temporary file next to DATA_FILE that is never removed
defects.repro: DATA_FILE=/tmp/x/d.json PORT=4000 node server.js; create group g; loop POST /groups/g/expenses {"payer":"Ann","cents":2,"split":"equal"} from two clients and send SIGKILL to the server mid-stream; ls /tmp/x; restart and ls again
defects.observed: d.json parses and is complete, but d.json.<uuid>.tmp remains in the directory, also after restart
defects.expected: No stray files, or leftover temporary files cleaned up at startup

defects.title: A group with a very long id is created (201) but can never be used: every group route answers 431 or drops the connection
defects.repro: Start the server. ID=$(printf "x%.0s" $(seq 1 20000)); curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST localhost:$PORT/groups -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"id\":\"$ID\",\"members\":[\"A\",\"B\"]}"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" localhost:$PORT/groups/$ID/balances
defects.observed: POST /groups -> 201 and the group is written to DATA_FILE; GET /groups/<id>/balances, POST /groups/<id>/expenses and GET /groups/<id>/settlements -> 431 (a 100,000-character id: connection reset). The id is taken, so it can never be recreated or used.
defects.expected: Either refuse ids too long to address (400) or keep every group that got 201 reachable by all three routes.
